title: Ship v1
summary: Repo up and agent-ready, cloud and CI/CD wired, errors and analytics watched from the first deploy.

parts.title: Set up a code hosting org
parts.guidance: Create the company-controlled repository organization, access model and initial project structure. Use the code-hosting workflow to verify contributor permissions and protect the intended development path. Retain setup and recovery ownership so the first release can be traced to reviewed source without depending on a single developer's personal account.

parts.title: Make the repo agent-ready
parts.guidance: Give agents the repository setup, project instructions and verification commands they need for a real contribution. Run a representative task in the available environment and fix missing instructions exposed by the attempt. Document supported operations, access boundaries and remaining failures so the next contribution can reach a reviewable diff with meaningful test evidence.

parts.title: Set up cloud infrastructure
parts.guidance: Choose infrastructure for the application's real runtime, data, networking and operational requirements. Follow the cloud workflow to provision the approved design and verify access, configuration and recovery arrangements. Keep environment details and ownership documented, distinguishing a created resource from a working application environment that the delivery pipeline can safely target.

parts.title: Set up CI/CD
parts.guidance: Configure the delivery pipeline around the repository, required checks and intended environments. Use the CI/CD workflow to test a controlled change through build, verification and authorized deployment, including failure handling. Preserve the pipeline result and release controls so the first live rollout has a reproducible path and a clear person responsible for approval.

parts.title: Set up error tracking
parts.guidance: Instrument the first release's important failure paths with useful context and appropriate data filtering. Use the error-tracking workflow to trigger a controlled error and verify that the right owner receives actionable evidence. Retain the tested alert path and triage expectations so launch issues can be diagnosed without collecting unnecessary sensitive information.

parts.title: Set up product analytics
parts.guidance: Define the first product questions and the events needed to answer them before enabling measurement. Implement and verify those events through the analytics workflow on the actual release. Check event definitions, privacy choices and duplicate-event handling, then give the launch team a baseline tied to the questions it needs to answer.
